negative_findings.description: No public, documented API was found for the official Hungarian registers in this cell — neither e-cegjegyzek.hu, e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu, cegkozlony.hu nor MNB Intézménykereső surfaced API documentation in hu or en searches.

coverage_gaps.description: The free e-Cégjegyzék service explicitly excludes acquiring all or a significant part of the register, and the beszámoló bulk dataset is sold commercially — the permissible automated collection volume is undefined.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Obtain the Céginformációs Szolgálat terms in writing and, if volume collection is needed, budget for the licensed dataset instead of scraping.

coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a per-institution crawl list of 'közérdekű adatok / 3.4 ötmillió forint feletti szerződések' pages for the public bodies most likely to buy payments services.

brief: Hungary's register layer for banking and payments is unusually well-consolidated: MNB's Intézménykereső, market-participant search, intermediary register, open-banking PSP list and Aranykönyv together enumerate and size every licensed bank, payment institution, e-money issuer and agent, with the EBA PSD2 central register providing the same universe in bulk-downloadable form. Identity and money then resolve through the Ministry of Justice stack — e-Cégjegyzék for legal identity, e-beszámoló for annual reports whose notes often disclose IT capex, outsourcing and contract values, and Cégközlöny for corporate-event flow — supplemented by NAV's free tax-status databases for validation and bidder eligibility. None of these expose a documented API: expect polite HTML collection, an emailed grouped-query form for beszámoló, or a licensed dataset from the Céginformációs Szolgálat or OPTEN, and note that the free company-register tier explicitly forbids bulk acquisition. For actual contract evidence outside formal tender portals, the üvegzseb regime (net HUF 5m+ contracts, indexed at kozadat.hu but authoritative on each institution's own disclosure page) is the register-side complement to the procurement cells.
